stories.headline: CU Boulder student killed, another critically injured in shooting after house party
stories.summary:
A 19-year-old University of Colorado student was shot and killed overnight Saturday, and another 19-year-old was critically injured, following a house party in the 700 block of Marine Street in Boulder. Boulder Police Chief Stephen Redfearn said it is the city's first homicide of the year.

Police received a noise complaint about the party, which included a live band and was attended by hundreds of people, at about 9:54 p.m. Officers shut it down within minutes and the crowd dispersed, but a core group stayed. Calls about a shooting began at 11:28 p.m., and officers found two people with gunshot wounds who were taken to Boulder Community Health.

Police are seeking two persons of interest who they believe were present when a group tried to force its way into the home, shortly before the shooting. Redfearn said there is no indication the suspects remain in Boulder, and about 20 witnesses were interviewed. Anyone with information or photos and video from the party is asked to call 303-441-3333.

stories.headline: One killed, one injured in separate Halloween shootings in Denver
stories.summary:
Two separate Halloween shootings in Denver left one person dead and another injured, according to the Denver Police Department. The first occurred in the 2600 block of North Federal Boulevard at about 6:33 p.m. Saturday, where a man died at the scene.

Thomas Callender, 43, was arrested on suspicion of first-degree murder, felony menacing and intimidating a witness or victim, according to Denver inmate records. He was being held without bail at the Downtown Detention Center as of Sunday. The Denver Office of the Medical Examiner will identify the victim.

Officers also responded to a shooting near East 52nd Avenue and Ventura Street, reported around 7:40 p.m. Paramedics took one victim to a hospital with unspecified injuries. Police said the investigation is ongoing.

stories.headline: San Juan River in Pagosa Springs forecast to top 1911 flood record; more than 1,000 homes under evacuation orders
stories.summary:
Authorities urged residents in parts of southwestern Colorado to evacuate Sunday as the San Juan River in Pagosa Springs was forecast to rise well above the 17.8-foot crest of the 1911 flood that destroyed much of the town. The National Weather Service forecast a crest of 21.84 feet by 11 p.m. Sunday, nearly 7 feet above last week's peak of about 15 feet.

Archuleta County Sheriff Mike Le Roux said more than 1,000 homes were under mandatory evacuation orders, many of them also evacuated during last week's storm. The county issued a shelter-in-place order asking residents to avoid nonessential travel. San Juan County ordered evacuations for anyone within a half-mile of the La Plata, San Juan or Animas rivers.

Incident commander Charles Balke said saturated ground has little capacity to absorb more rain, and smaller creeks are also flooding, causing unexpected road closures. He said evacuation is the top priority because swift-water rescue teams will struggle to reach people during intense rain.

stories.headline: Denver7 and Scripps Howard fund open donations for southwest Colorado flood victims
stories.summary:
Denver7 and the Scripps Howard fund have teamed up to raise money for victims of historic flooding in southwest Colorado. Multiple communities have issued mandatory evacuation orders or urged residents to leave as river levels were forecast to climb above historic marks.

The National Weather Service has a flood warning in effect through Monday evening with a "Particularly Dangerous Situation" tag. The San Juan River at Pagosa Springs was forecast to crest as high as 19.71 feet Sunday night, nearly 2 feet above the 17.8-foot crest of the 1911 flood.

Donations can be made through the Denver7 Gives page or by texting DENVER7GIVES to 50155.

stories.headline: Rain and cooler weather arrive in Denver as mountains brace for heavy snow
stories.summary:
A moisture-rich storm system is bringing showers to the Denver metro area, with snow increasing over the mountains. Monday will be cooler and wetter on the Front Range, with scattered to numerous rain showers across the plains and breezy to windy north winds.

In the mountains, snow levels are expected to drop to around 8,000 to 8,500 feet, with 5 to 10 inches forecast and the heaviest amounts in the northern mountains. Mountain roads could become slick, especially over passes. The National Weather Service said a high-end scenario, with a 10% chance, could bring up to 19 inches near the Eisenhower-Johnson Memorial Tunnel, versus about six inches in the more likely scenario.

Showers taper off Monday night, with a few flakes possible around the Palmer Divide. Tuesday should be mostly dry, with another weak system possible Wednesday.

stories.headline: Denver Post outlines Election Day coverage as Colorado polls close at 7 p.m. Tuesday
stories.summary:
Colorado polls close at 7 p.m. MST on Nov. 3, and the Denver Post said it will publish results drawn from the Colorado Secretary of State's office, relying on the Associated Press to call races.

Contests include governor, attorney general and secretary of state, U.S. House and Senate races, and a Denver City Council vacancy election. Voters will also decide statewide ballot propositions and amendments, measures in Denver, Aurora and Douglas County, and school mill levy overrides in Denver, Jeffco and Douglas County.

The newspaper noted that some winners may not be clear on Tuesday night and said results pages will update until every ballot is counted.

stories.headline: Colorado governor's race: Weiser favored over Marx as Lopez runs unaffiliated
stories.summary:
Gov. Jared Polis is term-limited, and Attorney General Phil Weiser, a Democrat, is heavily favored to succeed him against Republican Victor Marx, a Marine veteran and ministry leader. Democrats have held the office since 2007.

Weiser is campaigning on 40,000 starter homes, down-payment aid, K-12 funding, youth mental health and reforming TABOR. At an Oct. 8 Colorado Chamber forum he said he would sign a bill easing the Labor Peace Act's second-election requirement. Marx favors faster housing approvals, audits of state agencies and no new taxes, and said he would veto the labor bill.

Marx declined the Colorado Sun's debate invitation. Former U.S. Rep. Greg Lopez, a former Republican, is running as an unaffiliated candidate, along with Libertarian Eric Mulder and three other candidates.

stories.headline: Economist: Colorado's business climate faces headwinds amid fuel costs, high rates and slowing job growth
stories.summary:
Tatiana Bailey, executive director of the Colorado Springs-based Data-Driven Economic Strategies, wrote that national and state conditions are unusually uncertain. She cited diesel near $6.40 a gallon, a roughly 7.5% 30-year mortgage rate and inflation pressures tied to Middle East conflict and tariffs.

Colorado faces added challenges, she wrote, including high housing costs that make attracting workers harder and slower job growth after years of outperforming the nation. A Colorado Chamber of Commerce survey found 67% of businesses believe the state is headed in the wrong direction.

Bailey will present at the group's State of the Economy event Wednesday from 2 to 4 p.m. at Garden of the Gods Resort, with state labor market and Chamber officials also speaking.

stories.headline: Appeals court: pedestrian path where man fell is not a 'sidewalk' under Colorado law
stories.summary:
The Colorado Court of Appeals ruled Oct. 29 that a pedestrian pathway at Northeastern Junior College in Sterling is not a "sidewalk" under the Colorado Governmental Immunity Act, barring a negligence claim by a man who tripped on a 2.5-inch concrete deviation.

Gerald McBride, 75 at the time, fell in August 2022 while walking between an event center and a parking lot. A district court had allowed his suit to proceed, but the three-judge panel said the law defines a sidewalk as part of a public roadway, a point the lower court did not evaluate.

Judge Sueanna Johnson wrote that appellate decisions over 30 years have been inconsistent and that it may be time for the General Assembly to revisit the definition.

stories.headline: Broncos rally past Chiefs 28-24 on final-play goal-line stand to take AFC West lead
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos came back from a 24-13 fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Kansas City Chiefs 28-24 at Empower Field at Mile High. Malcolm Roach sacked Patrick Mahomes on fourth-and-goal on the final play, preserving the win.

Bo Nix threw two touchdown passes, both on fourth down, and finished with 222 yards. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman had a 51-yard catch and a 5-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. Kicker Wil Lutz set an NFL record with his 113th consecutive extra point since the league moved the distance back in 2015.

The fourth straight win moved Denver to 6-2 and into first place in the AFC West ahead of Kansas City at 5-2. Coach Sean Payton received a game ball for his 200th career win.

stories.headline: Colorado beats Kansas State 27-24 in overtime at Folsom Field
stories.summary:
The Colorado Buffaloes defeated Kansas State 27-24 in overtime at Folsom Field. Colorado's running backs carried 37 times for 218 yards and three touchdowns in the victory.

Ralphie VII led the Buffaloes out for the first run of the day before the game.

stories.headline: Avalanche to face Valeri Nichushkin for first time Tuesday in Columbus
stories.summary:
The Colorado Avalanche will play forward Valeri Nichushkin for the first time since trading him to the Columbus Blue Jackets, with the game set for Tuesday in Columbus. He is scheduled to return to Ball Arena in mid-February.

Nichushkin served two costly suspensions during his time in Denver, including one in the 2024 playoffs that came as the Avalanche were facing Dallas. The organization stood behind him and helped him rehabilitate, and he played two seasons without incident.

The Avalanche sent him to Columbus for draft picks and cap flexibility, citing salary-cap realities and his age and contract.

topStory.headline: Sen. Chris Murphy Hospitalized After Stroke, Aides Say He Is Responding Well to Treatment
topStory.summary:
Connecticut Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy, 53, was hospitalized after suffering a stroke on Saturday, his office said. Murphy began feeling numbness in his arm while attending his son's hockey game and was taken to a hospital, where doctors confirmed the stroke. He has since been transferred to Johns Hopkins for monitoring.

In a statement, Murphy's chief of staff, Allison Herwitt, said he is responding well to treatment. "The doctors are encouraged by his progress, he is awake and alert, and we are optimistic he will make a full recovery," the statement said. Connecticut Lt. Gov. Susan Bysiewicz said she was with Murphy on Friday evening, when he was encouraging voters to participate in the upcoming election, and said she was glad to hear he is doing well.

Sen. John Fetterman, a Pennsylvania Democrat who survived a near-fatal stroke, offered his support on X on Sunday. "As someone who survived a near-fatal stroke, I understand all too well how much this impacts your life," he wrote, adding that his family was rooting for Murphy and his family. Other senators have had health scares in recent years, including Maryland Democrat Chris Van Hollen and New Mexico Democrat Ben Ray Luján, who both had strokes in 2022. Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell, the former majority leader, was absent from the Capitol for months earlier this year after a fall.

Murphy was first elected to Congress in 2006 and has served in the Senate since 2013. He has been one of the most prominent voices for gun reform since the 2012 Sandy Hook school shooting and has also championed affordable health care and international human rights. He is not up for re-election this cycle, but has been campaigning for Democratic candidates, with recent stops in Michigan, Minnesota and Florida. He had been scheduled to travel to New Hampshire on Sunday.

Murphy is viewed by some observers as a possible 2028 presidential candidate because of his outspoken opposition to President Donald Trump. In a 2025 interview with the Guardian, he said anyone focused on the 2028 or 2026 elections would be foolish, arguing that energy should go toward protecting democracy. His absence from the campaign trail comes as Democrats try to take control of Congress from Republicans, who hold the majority in both chambers. No timeline has been given for his discharge or return to campaigning.
